item.title: Styling with CSS
item.description: Lesson 2: Styling with CSS CSS, Cascading Style Sheets, controls how HTML looks: colours, fonts, spacing, and layout. Keeping CSS separate from HTML is good practice. HTML says "this is a heading"; CSS says "headings in this section use this font and size". That separation means you can change the…

item.description: Lesson 3: Layout with Flexbox and Grid Early web layout relied on tricks such as tables and floated boxes, which were never designed for page layout and made responsive design painful. item.title: The DOM — Making Pages Respond
item.description: Lesson 5: The DOM — Making Pages Respond The Document Object Model, or DOM, is the browser's live representation of your HTML as a tree of objects that JavaScript can read and change. When JavaScript changes the DOM, the page on screen changes without reloading. That is how menus open, messages…

item.title: Forms, Input, and Validation
item.description: Lesson 6: Forms, Input, and Validation Forms are how users send information to a site: sign-ups, contact messages, orders, and searches. A form is built from <form>, labelled controls such as <input>, <textarea>, and <select>, and a submit button. Good forms are usable, accessible, and validated in…

item.title: Responsive Design and Accessibility
item.description: Lesson 7: Responsive Design and Accessibility A responsive page works on a phone, a tablet, and a desktop, not by shrinking a desktop layout until it is unreadable, but by adapting its layout to the space available. Accessibility means the same page works for people using keyboards, screen readers…
